purpose: Screen fixed, scientifically motivated receptor-ensemble objectives for classical transfer, effective energy gaps, and coefficient-noise robustness before any quantum-hardware execution.

noise_models.description: Additive Gaussian noise with standard deviation equal to noise_level times the max-absolute scaled coefficient.
Multiplicative Gaussian noise with standard deviation equal to noise_level times each scaled coefficient magnitude.

candidates.rationale: An active ligand counts when at least one selected receptor ranks it in the frozen early-rank band.
An active ligand must be supported by at least two selected receptor conformations.
An active ligand must be supported by all three selected receptor conformations.
Two-hit active consensus with an explicit penalty for positively correlated receptor scores.

algorithm.active_encoding: threshold*y_active + slack = sum_i incidence_ai*x_i; negative active coefficient selects y_active when threshold is feasible
algorithm.decoy_encoding: z_decoy >= x_i for every receptor i exposing the decoy; positive decoy coefficient penalizes exposure
algorithm.objective: weighted active threshold coverage - decoy_weight*weighted decoy exposure - redundancy_weight*mean positive score correlation
algorithm.selection_solver: enumerate all 560 receptor triples with the lowest-energy feasible auxiliary assignment
algorithm.noise_model: independent Gaussian perturbation of every nonconstant QUBO coefficient after max-absolute scaling; feasibility is evaluated through reconstructed auxiliary assignments

requirements: candidate beats direct greedy with positive mean delta on both targets and at least five positive folds out of eight
candidate has scaled best-versus-second-best feasible energy gap at least hardware_gap_threshold_scaled on both targets
candidate retains the same selected triple in at least hardware_stability_threshold of 5-percent trials under both absolute-full-scale and relative-coefficient noise on both targets
hardware_readiness_gate.decision_boundary: This screen can authorize only a separately preregistered hardware pilot; it never amends a prior validation gate or establishes quantum advantage.

interpretation_boundary: Stage 19i is a post-hoc train-only design review over MK14 and PPARG. It adds no docking and reads no fresh-validation, locked-test, or BACE1 rows. A passing candidate would be a hardware-readiness signal only; a failure means the candidate is not ready for hardware, not that all quantum approaches are impossible.
